old.name: 🌉 Le péristyle · minuit en novembre
old.hook: Heart of Diocletian's Palace · after 23:30 — cold Egyptian marbles · a 1500 BC sphinx
old.text: Heart of Diocletian's Palace · after 23:30 — cold Egyptian marbles · a 1500 BC sphinx Diocletian's peristyle is the palace's central court (305 AD). In tourist daytime, it's a scrum. But at midnight in November, after the last waiters leave, you can sit on the Vestibule steps, beneath the Egyptian black-granite sphinx (15th c. BC, reused by Diocletian). The marble keeps the sea's cold. The acoustic resonance is made for voice: this is where the klape sing a cappella in summer.

old.name: 🏔 Plage Bačvice
old.hook: 10-min walk from centre · free — urban sand beach · Dalmatian picigin
old.text: 10-min walk from centre · free — urban sand beach · Dalmatian picigin Sand beach (rare in Dalmatia where everything is pebbles), 10 min walk from the center. Shallow water — you can walk 30 m offshore without going over the waist. This is where picigin is played — a Dalmatian beach sport: pass a small ball by slapping the water with the palm, never letting it drop, with diving saves. Croatian intangible heritage sport. A late-afternoon show to watch.

old.name: Palais de Dioclétien
old.hook: UNESCO 1979 · free — 215 × 180 m rectangular plan, 4th c.
old.text: UNESCO 1979 · free — 215 × 180 m rectangular plan, 4th c. Free (access) · €4–6 for cathedral, substructures, baptistery See the funfact. Four original gates: Golden Gate (north), Silver Gate (east), Bronze Gate (south, sea-facing), Iron Gate (west). The peristyle (colonnaded court) at the heart. The substructures are almost entirely preserved — Game of Thrones episodes 8–10 were filmed here. Cathedral (Diocletian's former octagonal mausoleum, ironically reconverted to a Christian church in the 7th century), Temple of Jupiter (now the baptistery). What to see Peristyle · substructures · cathedral · baptistery

old.name: Cathédrale Saint-Domnius
old.text: Palace · €4–6 — Diocletian's former mausoleum, 4th c. Octagonal mausoleum built by Diocletian (himself a persecutor of Christians) to house his own tomb. In the 7th century reconverted into a Christian cathedral and named after Saint Domnius (Sveti Duje), bishop martyr of Salona, killed in the Diocletianic persecution — perfect historical irony. 13th-c. Romanesque bell tower (60 m, paid climb, panorama over palace and bay). Carved-wood doors by Andrija Buvina (1214). Treasury. What to see Mausoleum · bell tower · Buvina doors

old_also.name: 🏛 Toits du palais depuis le campanile de Saint-Domnius
old_also.hook: Cathedral · Romanesque-Gothic bell tower · morning — the Roman grid still readable · Mosor in the distance
old_also.text: Cathedral · Romanesque-Gothic bell tower · morning — the Roman grid still readable · Mosor in the distance The campanile of St Domnius (13th–16th c., rebuilt in the 19th) dominates the palace. Climb at opening (8am): you see the Roman grid of the palace, still perfectly legible 1,700 years later, and behind it the Mosor massif (1,339 m), often snow-capped in winter. €7. Steep stairs — not for claustrophobes, even less for vertigo sufferers. Empty until 9:30am. When 08:00–09:00

old.text: North centre · €4–6 — oldest museum in Croatia (1820) The oldest museum in Croatia, founded 1820. Roman collection (mosaics, statues, sarcophagi, artefacts from Salona, the former Roman capital of Dalmatia 5 km north of Split), Greek (Issa, the ancient Greek colony on Vis), Illyrian. The 4th-century Good Shepherd sarcophagus is one of the highlights. What to see Good Shepherd sarcophagus · Roman Salona · Greek Issa

old.text: Foot of Marjan (15-min walk from centre) · €8–10 — house-studio of Ivan Meštrović, Croatia's 20th-c. sculptor 8–10 € Ivan Meštrović (1883–1962), the great 20th-century Croatian sculptor, a Rodin student, built this villa in Split in 1939 as a house-studio. Today a museum. Monumental sculptures (Mother and Son, Cycle of Job), bas-reliefs, drawings. Combine with Kaštelet-Crikvine Meštrović 200 m away (a chapel decorated with a wood-bas-relief cycle). What to see House-studio · monumental sculptures · chapel
